title: Opposite canonical derived tensor symmetries cancel
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme and $\Lambda$ any commutative ring. Let $K,M$ be objects of the unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ of ordinary étale $\Lambda$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived tensor product [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Write $\sigma_{K,M}:K\otimes^L_\Lambda M\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes^L_\Lambda K$ for the fixed canonical signed symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym]. Then $\sigma_{M,K}\circ\sigma_{K,M}=\operatorname{id}_{K\otimes^L_\Lambda M}$. No boundedness, characteristic, finiteness or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For cochain complexes K,M, use the coproduct universal property to test the double braiding on each summand K.X p tensor M.X q. Apply CochainComplex.Monoidal.ι_braiding_hom twice. Coefficient-category symmetry cancels the two ordinary braidings, and Int.units_coe_mul_self cancels the two identical signs after commuting p*q and q*p. Thus the composite is identity in each degree, hence as a cochain map.

Every homotopy-category object is represented by a cochain complex. The canonical homotopy braiding is the quotient image of the cochain braiding. Functoriality therefore carries the double-swap identity to the homotopy category, and Iso.inv_ext' identifies the opposite hom with the inverse.

Apply Functor.leftDerived₂_ext to the two canonical derived lifts braidingNatTrans and braidingInvNatTrans. Their factorization equations differ only by the homotopy braiding hom versus the opposite inverse, already equal by the preceding step. The lifts are equal. Replace the second braiding in the desired composite by the inverse lift and apply the existing braidingNatTrans_comp_braidingInvNatTrans component identity. Specialize to ordinary etale module sheaves. Package the double-swap equation as the private predicate swapInvolutive on the whole natural isomorphism. Rewrite canonicalTensorSymmetry_eq at that level, then specialize the proved generic property to sheaves and modules. This avoids repeated unfolding of component monoidal instances and changes no map.

mathlib_searches.query: The canonical braiding on the derived tensor product of sheaves of modules is involutive: swapping the two factors twice gives the identity.
The braiding on the unbounded derived tensor product of module sheaves is symmetric, so the composite of the two opposite canonical swaps is the identity.

theorem derivedTensorSymmetry_involutive
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u})
    (K M : DerivedCategoryModule Λ X) :
    ((derivedTensorSymmetry (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) X).hom.app K).app M ≫
      ((derivedTensorSymmetry (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) X).hom.app M).app K = 𝟙 _
